description: 2 tactical challenges for Black against the Smith-Morra Gambit. Meet 2.d4 with solid development and return the pawn at the right moment.

drills.briefExplanation: 2...cxd4 3.c3 dxc3 4.Nxc3 Nc6 5.Nf3 d6 — accept the pawn, develop solidly, and give it back for equality.
drills.description: Black to play. White gambits with 2.d4 — accept it and find the solid setup.
drills.explanation: Against the Morra, Black's best policy is: take the pawn, develop, and return it when convenient. After 2...cxd4 3.c3 dxc3 4.Nxc3 Nc6 Black develops the knight first — the key move, fighting for d4 and e5. 5...d6 solidifies e5, and after the coming ...e6, ...Nf6, ...Be7 Black will be a tempo down but structurally sound, ready to neutralize White's initiative.
drills.name: Weathering the Gambit

drills.briefExplanation: 3...dxc3 4.Nxc3 Nc6 5.Nf3 d6 6.Bc4 e6 7.O-O Nf6 — develop knights before bishops and keep the center flexible.
drills.description: Black to play. White has offered the c-pawn with 3.c3 — take it and develop the Maroczy-style setup.
drills.explanation: 3...dxc3 accepts the second pawn, and now 4...Nc6 is the cornerstone — development with central control. The setup 5...d6, 6...e6, 7...Nf6 follows the Scheveningen pattern: Black concedes space but keeps every break (...d5, ...b5) in reserve. White's initiative looks scary but evaporates against accurate, patient defense.
drills.name: Developing Calmly
